problem: Separate language/video planning from environment-specific action generation to share task knowledge across different control tasks.
contribution: UniPi instantiates the Unified Predictive Decision Process with a first-frame/text-conditioned video planner and a separately trained inverse dynamics decoder. A universal visual interface reduces representation differences but does not remove the need for robot-specific action supervision.
algorithm: Train diffusion video generation with explicit first-frame context tiled across every future frame; synthesize coarse temporal plans then temporal-super-resolve. T5 encodes instructions and classifier-free guidance controls conditioning. Train a small inverse model independently from labeled transitions. Paper experiments execute inferred action sequence open-loop for computational efficiency, although closed-loop regeneration is discussed as possible.
observations: Initial image and task text for planner; generated adjacent frames for action decoder. Planning datasets need video/task pairs and decoder needs actual actions. Web video priors encode plausible visual behavior, not force or calibrated reachability.
actions: Task-specific continuous joint/control actions inferred from video; inverse model can be trained on smaller/suboptimal simulator data. Video generation alone does not command a new robot embodiment.
embodiment_and_data: Scripted block-coloring/placement and multitask simulation,200k videos per setting with70/30instruction split; ten train/three test tasks for transfer. Real-domain study usesBridge7.2kvideo-text pairs80/20split plus14Mvideo-text/60Mimage-text/LAION400Mpretraining. Original large pretrained initialization is not independently reproduced here.
experiments: Combinatorial simulation task completion, first-frame/tiling/hierarchy ablations, multienvironment task transfer and real-domain video generation. Real-domain Table4 success is a final-frame classifier judgment on generated videos, not actual hardware rollouts. No measured physical deployment success is established in inspected main experiments.
baselines: State/Image TransformerBC,ImageTrajectoryTransformer and action-spaceDiffuser with sharedT5 conditions; video model from scratch versus internetpretraining. Baselines use continuous actions rather than preprogrammed pick/place primitives.
quantitative_result: Table1 PDFp6 novel place60.1±3.9%,relation46.1±3.0%UniPi versus13.2±4.1/9.1±2.5ImageTT. Table3p8 heldout placebowl51.6±3.6%,packobject75.5±3.1%,packpair45.7±3.7%. Table4p9 generated-video success77.1%pretrained versus72.6%scratch; explicitly a classifier proxy, not physicalsuccess.
limitations: Open-loop execution accumulates errors; plausible video can be physically inconsistent or beyond inverse-model support. Real-domain video scores do not validate embodied execution. Web-scale initialization/data and target-specific inverse actions limit reproducibility and novel-robot claims. Language replaces explicit reward specification but cannot prove task validity.
code_and_license: Primary project https://universal-policy.github.io/ . Independent implementation/checkpoint and constituent dataset license audits not performed; no code inspected/executed. Proprietary pretrained model availability should not be assumed from later reimplementations.
hardware_adaptation: COMPARE video-plan/inverse-decoder abstraction against a small calibrated simulation baseline; preserve actual action labels and IK feasibility. Current SO101/ROSMASTER transfer is geometry engineering, not a UniPi policy. Generated-video success never qualifies as observed physical or handover success.
